facts.heading: GP suggested therapy visit
facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he come to therapy because she noticed he looked exhausted.
facts.evidence: My GP suggested I come. She said I look exhausted, and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's company lost a big client, and he ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Works long hours
facts.content: Daniel starts work at seven and continues answering messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night.

facts.heading: Sleep is terrible
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Dreading nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights.
facts.evidence: I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's condition details
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.

facts.heading: Appointments are bi-weekly
facts.content: The neurology appointments are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: The neurology appointments are every few weeks,

facts.heading: Caregiving burden falls on Daniel
facts.content: Daniel is the one responsible for the care of his father because his younger sister lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Feels guilty about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Tells sister he is fine
facts.content: Daniel tells his sister Hannah that he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Cannot face hospital visits
facts.content: Daniel sometimes sits in the hospital car park for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.heading: GP found blood tests normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP ran blood tests, and they were all normal.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal.

facts.heading: GP attributed issues to stress
facts.content: Daniel's GP said his issues were due to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy appointment
facts.content: Claire booked the therapy appointment for Daniel.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Claire concerned about Daniel
facts.content: Claire is concerned because she feels she is 'done watching him disappear'.
facts.evidence: She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire is patient but strained
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes Daniel tea, but Daniel sees that it is wearing on her.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk. But I can see it's wearing on her too.

facts.heading: Stopped weekend trips with Claire
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend

facts.heading: Daniel avoids trips due to emails
facts.content: Daniel avoids going away because he anticipates returning to two hundred emails.
facts.evidence: The emails. If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them.

facts.heading: Daniel worries about Dad's needs
facts.content: Daniel is concerned that his Dad might need something while he is away.
facts.evidence: And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Last time properly off
facts.content: Daniel cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran 10km for six years
facts.content: Daniel used to run ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead

facts.heading: Boss sends late night emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at eleven at night.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Boss expects early reply
facts.content: Daniel's boss expects an answer to emails before breakfast.
facts.evidence: and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers boss's emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even if he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as uncommitted
facts.content: Daniel fears his boss will think he is not committed if he doesn't answer emails.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss in spring
facts.content: Daniel is afraid he might be let go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Mortgage is a financial concern
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Reported flat and irritable mood
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Snapped at colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing

facts.heading: Experienced heart symptoms in toilet
facts.content: Daniel felt his heart was racing and his hands were shaking in the toilet.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Experiences on train to Manchester
facts.content: Daniel experienced an incident on the train to Manchester where he had to get off and stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Has not told Claire about incident
facts.content: Daniel has not told Claire about the incident he experienced.
facts.evidence: I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Fears losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that he is losing control and not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coffee intake is six cups daily
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee per day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Uses wine in evenings to switch off
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings to distract himself.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Drinks two to three glasses of wine
facts.content: Daniel drinks two or sometimes three glasses of wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Feels uneasy about wine use
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about his wine consumption.
facts.evidence: Uneasy.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing his feelings.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Sleep is the biggest concern
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather worked in Yorkshire mines
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire.

facts.heading: Family pattern of not complaining
facts.content: Daniel notes that his grandfather and father never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same.

facts.heading: Feels pressure from grandfather's view
facts.content: Daniel worries his grandfather would think he was weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Believes he is tired, not weak
facts.content: Daniel states that he is tired, not weak.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Agrees to try small change
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try a small change regarding his phone use.
facts.evidence: Yes.

facts.heading: Plans to try phone switch-off
facts.content: Daniel plans to try switching off his phone at half past nine with Claire.
facts.evidence: Half past nine, perhaps. I could make it a thing with Claire.

facts.heading: Will track sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down when he wakes up regarding his sleep.
facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Attendance at next session
facts.content: Daniel will attend the next session next week.
facts.evidence: Yes. I'll be here.

facts.heading: Difficulty with train travel
facts.content: Daniel finds the trains to be awful.
facts.evidence: the trains are awful.
